title: Opportunistic SSE patch tokens and idempotent reconnect for compact streaming
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement: The current SSE resume strategies rely on large per-session snapshots or long resume tokens which increase memory and bandwidth for high-concurrency customers and complicate structured tool-call boundaries. We need a lightweight, backward-compatible reconnect approach that minimizes server state, preserves function/tool-call atomicity across partial deliveries, and reduces worst-case retransmit size for mobile and constrained clients.

Goal: Design and implement an "opportunistic patch" protocol layered on top of existing SSE endpoints that: (1) emits compact per-chunk stable markers and small checkpoints (patch anchors), (2) provides an idempotency-style reconnect handshake so clients and servers agree on replay deltas, (3) encodes semantic boundary hints for function/tool-call start/finish to avoid broken JSON/structured outputs on reconnect, and (4) remains compatible with existing non-upgraded clients (graceful degradation).
acceptance_criteria: SSE endpoints can emit compact per-chunk 'patch-anchor' headers without changing the top-level event format (compatible with current clients)
On reconnect, clients may provide the last-seen anchor token; server responds with either a short patch (delta) or a stateless resume index plus minimal instructions to re-request missing fragments
Function/tool-call boundaries are preserved: downstream consumer receives either a complete tool-call or an explicit 'aborted-marker' so callers can safely retry invocation logic
End-to-end tests demonstrate at least 40% reduction in bytes retransmitted during typical reconnects vs full-session resend for a mixed workload (chat + tool calls + JSON blocks)
Feature is behind a runtime flag and can be toggled per-model and per-customer; non-participating clients see identical stream payloads (no regression)
Observability hooks emit resume metrics (resume_requested, patch_sent_bytes, skipped_retransmits) and alert on abnormal patch failure rates (>1% across 1h)
Security review completed for token formats and no new sensitive material is leaked by patch anchors
design_notes:
High-level approach: embed a small, URL-safe 'patch-anchor' token in chunk metadata header (base64url, 16 bytes entropy) and include semantic 'boundary' hints that are optional and freeform (e.g. 'fn:start:order-summary'). Anchors are generated deterministically from chunk provenance (session id, sequence id, sha128(chunk)) so server can regenerate anchors with minimal retained state.

Reconnect handshake: client reconnects and sends ?resume_anchor=<token>. Server validates token by recomputing deterministic anchor and either: (A) if server still has recent segment cache -> return a concise patch payload (list of chunk ids and replacement bytes) in a single SSE 'patch' event; or (B) if cache is cold -> reply with 'resume-index' and instruct client which subsequent anchors to expect. Client merges patch onto local buffer; on function-call boundaries the server emits an explicit 'fn:abort' or 'fn:complete' sentinel when appropriate.

Compatibility considerations: if a client doesn't include resume_anchor, server behavior unchanged. Anchors are optional metadata fields encoded as an SSE comment line or small JSON envelope inside existing data chunk to avoid breaking simple line-parsed clients. For older clients we still include standard chunk content as first-class payload.

Tool/function-call semantics: introduce two small sentinel events that are idempotent by design: 'fn:begin:<id>' and 'fn:end:<id>:status' emitted as separate SSE events. When a reconnect occurs between begin and end, the server can choose to either replay the full tool-call output in the patch or emit 'fn:abort:<id>' to signal a retry-safe state. This avoids partial JSON fragments being misinterpreted by callers.
implementation_steps: RFC PR: add spec doc to docs/streaming/ops with token encoding, sentinel names, and reconnect handshake (engineering + PM review)
Runtime: add lightweight deterministic anchor generator to event writer (C++ runtime), feature-flagged behind 'sse.patch_anchors'
Server cache: add bounded LRU segment cache keyed by anchor id with TTL 30s for typical reconnect windows (configurable)
API: extend connection open flow to accept optional resume_anchor and return resume capability header; no schema change for existing payloads
Client SDKs: JavaScript and Python SDKs add reconnect helper to attach last-seen anchor and merge incoming 'patch' events (minor semver bump)
Tool-call sentinel: implement emit of 'fn:begin' and 'fn:end' SSE events in tool runner path; ensure serialization is atomic with chunk emission
E2E tests: harness that simulates flaky networks, mid-function disconnects, and validates structured JSON integrity after reconnect
Feature rollout flags exposed in Console (model-level and customer-level toggles)
test_plan: Unit tests for anchor generation (collision probability), deterministic recomputation, and expiration semantics. Integration tests: simulated reconnects at varying offsets (edge of chunk, mid-chunk, between fn begin/end). Load test: create 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with induced 0.5% reconnects and measure retransmit bytes and latency impact. SDK tests: ensure older SDKs gracefully ignore extra SSE comments or small JSON envelopes. Security fuzzing: malformed anchor tokens should fail gracefully and not expose internal state.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout on runtime-1.24: enable sse.patch_anchors for internal canary orgs and a small percent of new signups (10%). Monitor resume metrics and error rates for 48h. If stable, widen to 50% then GA. Provide rollback toggle for immediate disable. Coordinate SDK releases to be available before GA but allow non-SDK clients to opt-in manually.
monitoring_plan: Expose metrics: patch_anchor_generated, patch_anchor_served, patch_bytes_sent, resume_errors, fn_aborts, fn_replays. Dashboards: per-model and per-customer breakdown. Alerts: resume_errors > 1% or avg patch_bytes_sent > baseline+30% triggers PagerDuty. Add logging correlation id for each anchor so we can trace reconnect session lifecycle in logs.
risks_and_mitigations: State mismatch: deterministic anchors may collide if underlying input changes; mitigate by including sequence id + sha and a revision counter in anchor derivation
Privacy leakage: anchors might reveal chunk hashes; ensure anchors are opaque (HMAC with server-only key) and not reversible
Client parsing regressions: older clients may mis-handle new comment lines; ensure anchors are attached as SSE comments or optional JSON envelopes that are ignored by minimalist parsers
Operational cost: segment cache increases memory; bound by LRU and TTL and allow per-customer caps
